primitives.breakdown_regime: φ > θ_a when effort exceeds normal range due to paralysis.

primitives.name: Motor Effort Compensation
primitives.verbatim_quote: If that object be situated 20 degrees to the right, the patient has now to innervate as powerfully to turn the eye those 20 degrees as formerly he did to turn the eye 30 degrees.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'k': 'proportionality constant linking force and angular velocity (rad·s⁻¹·N⁻¹)', 'F(t)': 'time-varying innervation force (newtons)', 'θ': 'angular displacement (radians)'}
primitives.assumptions: Angular velocity scales inversely with muscle integrity; compensation increases exponentially with required rotation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As muscle strength decreases, F(t) must increase to maintain same θ, leading to overcompensation.

layer2.mapping: Compensatory motor strategy mimics inverse kinematics in robotic control systems; error accumulates due to non-linear force-displacement relationship.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized effort vs. angular displacement ratio during gaze shifts

The core operator governing eye movement perception is the sensory-motor feedback loop where innervation effort is misinterpreted as spatial accuracy. In healthy subjects, the brain interprets the 'feeling of innervation' as proportional to actual eye rotation. However, in paralysis cases, reduced muscle efficacy necessitates greater effort for equivalent motion, causing misalignment between perceived and actual angular displacement. This leads to a systematic overestimation of gaze direction. The mathematical structure reflects a nonlinear transformation: φ(θ_a) = θ_a + ε(F), where ε(F) captures the deviation due to effort scaling. The breakdown regime occurs when F approaches zero, rendering the system insensitive to changes in θ. Dualities emerge in how the same neural discharge pattern can imply either high or low effort depending on context. Failure modes include persistent overcompensation and inability to recalibrate spatial beliefs without retraining. These insights inform both GSI's probabilistic inference models and GSE's dynamic state transition logic.
